generation.domain: nonsingular real linear system; no exchanges; integer entries

question.:question/problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}-3x-6y-3z&=-3 \\ -x-4y-z&=5 \\ -x-y-3z&=-12\end{aligned}\right..
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}-3 & -6 & -3 & -3 \\ -1 & -4 & -1 & 5 \\ -1 & -1 & -3 & -12\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_1:=-\frac{1}{3}R_1$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & 1 & 1 \\ -1 & -4 & -1 & 5 \\ -1 & -1 & -3 & -12\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_2:=R_2+R_1$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & -2 & 0 & 6 \\ -1 & -1 & -3 & -12\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=R_3+R_1$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & -2 & 0 & 6 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & -11\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_2:=-\frac{1}{2}R_2$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & -11\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=R_3-R_2$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & -2 & -8\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=-\frac{1}{2}R_3$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 4\end{array}\right].
$$

The matrix is in row echelon form: each pivot lies to the right of the pivot above it, with zeros below each pivot.

The corresponding triangular system is

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x+2y+z&=1 \\ y&=-3 \\ z&=4\end{aligned}\right..
$$

Back substitution gives

$$
\begin{aligned}z&=4 \\ y&=-3-(0)(4)=-3 \\ x&=1-(2)(-3)-(1)(4)=3.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $\langle 3,-3,4\rangle$.

$$

$$

Using $R_2:=\frac{1}{3}R_2$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 0 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & -8 \\ 0 & -1 & 0 & 4\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=R_3+R_2$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 0 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & -8 \\ 0 & 0 & -2 & -4\end{array}\right].
$$

$$

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}2 & 0 & -4 & -2 \\ 1 & -3 & -2 & 8 \\ -2 & 2 & 1 & -1\end{array}\right].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}2 & 0 & -4 & -2 \\ 1 & -3 & -2 & 8 \\ -2 & 2 & 1 & -1\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_1:=\frac{1}{2}R_1$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 0 & -2 & -1 \\ 1 & -3 & -2 & 8 \\ -2 & 2 & 1 & -1\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_2:=R_2-R_1$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 0 & -2 & -1 \\ 0 & -3 & 0 & 9 \\ -2 & 2 & 1 & -1\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=R_3+2R_1$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 0 & -2 & -1 \\ 0 & -3 & 0 & 9 \\ 0 & 2 & -3 & -3\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_2:=-\frac{1}{3}R_2$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 0 & -2 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -3 \\ 0 & 2 & -3 & -3\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=R_3-2R_2$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 0 & -2 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & -3 & 3\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=-\frac{1}{3}R_3$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 0 & -2 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -1\end{array}\right].
$$

The matrix is in row echelon form: each pivot lies to the right of the pivot above it, with zeros below each pivot.

The corresponding triangular system is

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x-2z&=-1 \\ y&=-3 \\ z&=-1\end{aligned}\right..
$$

Back substitution gives

$$
\begin{aligned}z&=-1 \\ y&=-3-(0)(-1)=-3 \\ x&=-1-(0)(-3)-(-2)(-1)=-3.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $\langle -3,-3,-1\rangle$.

question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}-2 & 4 & 2 & 0 \\ -2 & 1 & 2 & -3 \\ 1 & -1 & -3 & -1\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_1:=-\frac{1}{2}R_1$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & -1 & 0 \\ -2 & 1 & 2 & -3 \\ 1 & -1 & -3 & -1\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_2:=R_2+2R_1$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & -3 & 0 & -3 \\ 1 & -1 & -3 & -1\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=R_3-R_1$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & -3 & 0 & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & -1\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_2:=-\frac{1}{3}R_2$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & -1\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=R_3-R_2$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & -2 & -2\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=-\frac{1}{2}R_3$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1\end{array}\right].
$$

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x-2y-z&=0 \\ y&=1 \\ z&=1\end{aligned}\right..

$$
\begin{aligned}z&=1 \\ y&=1-(0)(1)=1 \\ x&=0-(-2)(1)-(-1)(1)=3.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $\langle 3,1,1\rangle$.

$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}-2 & 2 & -2 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & -3 & 0 \\ -2 & 4 & -8 & -8\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_1:=-\frac{1}{2}R_1$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & -3 & 0 \\ -2 & 4 & -8 & -8\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_2:=R_2-R_1$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & -4 & 0 \\ -2 & 4 & -8 & -8\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=R_3+2R_1$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & -4 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & -6 & -8\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_2:=\frac{1}{2}R_2$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & -6 & -8\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=R_3-2R_2$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -2 & -8\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=-\frac{1}{2}R_3$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 4\end{array}\right].
$$

The matrix is in row echelon form: each pivot lies to the right of the pivot above it, with zeros below each pivot.

The corresponding triangular system is

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x-y+z&=0 \\ y-2z&=0 \\ z&=4\end{aligned}\right..
$$

Back substitution gives

$$
\begin{aligned}z&=4 \\ y&=0-(-2)(4)=8 \\ x&=0-(-1)(8)-(1)(4)=4.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $\langle 4,8,4\rangle$.

$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}3 & -3 & 6 & 12 \\ -1 & -2 & -5 & -7 \\ -1 & 2 & 1 & -9\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_1:=\frac{1}{3}R_1$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 2 & 4 \\ -1 & -2 & -5 & -7 \\ -1 & 2 & 1 & -9\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_2:=R_2+R_1$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 2 & 4 \\ 0 & -3 & -3 & -3 \\ -1 & 2 & 1 & -9\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=R_3+R_1$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 2 & 4 \\ 0 & -3 & -3 & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 & -5\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_2:=-\frac{1}{3}R_2$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 2 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 & -5\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=R_3-R_2$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 2 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & -6\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=\frac{1}{2}R_3$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 2 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -3\end{array}\right].
$$

The matrix is in row echelon form: each pivot lies to the right of the pivot above it, with zeros below each pivot.

The corresponding triangular system is

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x-y+2z&=4 \\ y+z&=1 \\ z&=-3\end{aligned}\right..
$$

Back substitution gives

$$
\begin{aligned}z&=-3 \\ y&=1-(1)(-3)=4 \\ x&=4-(-1)(4)-(2)(-3)=14.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $\langle 14,4,-3\rangle$.

question.:question/problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}3x-3y&=3 \\ -x+4y+3z&=8 \\ 2x+5z&=17\end{aligned}\right..
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}3 & -3 & 0 & 3 \\ -1 & 4 & 3 & 8 \\ 2 & 0 & 5 & 17\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_1:=\frac{1}{3}R_1$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 0 & 1 \\ -1 & 4 & 3 & 8 \\ 2 & 0 & 5 & 17\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_2:=R_2+R_1$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 3 & 3 & 9 \\ 2 & 0 & 5 & 17\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=R_3-2R_1$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 3 & 3 & 9 \\ 0 & 2 & 5 & 15\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_2:=\frac{1}{3}R_2$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 3 \\ 0 & 2 & 5 & 15\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=R_3-2R_2$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 3 & 9\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=\frac{1}{3}R_3$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 3\end{array}\right].
$$

The matrix is in row echelon form: each pivot lies to the right of the pivot above it, with zeros below each pivot.

The corresponding triangular system is

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x-y&=1 \\ y+z&=3 \\ z&=3\end{aligned}\right..
$$

Back substitution gives

$$
\begin{aligned}z&=3 \\ y&=3-(1)(3)=0 \\ x&=1-(-1)(0)-(0)(3)=1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $\langle 1,0,3\rangle$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 0 & -1 & 3 \\ 0 & -3 & 6 & -3 \\ 0 & -2 & 7 & 4\end{array}\right].

$$

$$

$$

M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}-2 & 0 & 4 & -6 \\ 2 & -2 & -6 & 14 \\ 1 & 2 & -2 & 3\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_1:=-\frac{1}{2}R_1$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 0 & -2 & 3 \\ 2 & -2 & -6 & 14 \\ 1 & 2 & -2 & 3\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_2:=R_2-2R_1$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 0 & -2 & 3 \\ 0 & -2 & -2 & 8 \\ 1 & 2 & -2 & 3\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=R_3-R_1$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 0 & -2 & 3 \\ 0 & -2 & -2 & 8 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 & 0\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_2:=-\frac{1}{2}R_2$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 0 & -2 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & -4 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 & 0\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=R_3-2R_2$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 0 & -2 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & -4 \\ 0 & 0 & -2 & 8\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=-\frac{1}{2}R_3$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 0 & -2 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & -4 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -4\end{array}\right].
$$

The matrix is in row echelon form: each pivot lies to the right of the pivot above it, with zeros below each pivot.

The corresponding triangular system is

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x-2z&=3 \\ y+z&=-4 \\ z&=-4\end{aligned}\right..
$$

Back substitution gives

$$
\begin{aligned}z&=-4 \\ y&=-4-(1)(-4)=0 \\ x&=3-(0)(0)-(-2)(-4)=-5.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $\langle -5,0,-4\rangle$.

knowledge_point.title: Solving a 3x3 System of Equations Using Standard Gaussian Elimination

generation.domain: nonsingular real linear system; no exchanges; integer entries

question.:question/problem:
Consider the augmented matrix

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}3 & -3 & 3 & 12 \\ -1 & -2 & -1 & -1 \\ -1 & -1 & 2 & 7\end{array}\right].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}3 & -3 & 3 & 12 \\ -1 & -2 & -1 & -1 \\ -1 & -1 & 2 & 7\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_1:=\frac{1}{3}R_1$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 1 & 4 \\ -1 & -2 & -1 & -1 \\ -1 & -1 & 2 & 7\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_2:=R_2+R_1$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & -3 & 0 & 3 \\ -1 & -1 & 2 & 7\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=R_3+R_1$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & -3 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & -2 & 3 & 11\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_2:=-\frac{1}{3}R_2$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & -2 & 3 & 11\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=R_3+2R_2$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 3 & 9\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=\frac{1}{3}R_3$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 3\end{array}\right].
$$

The matrix is in row echelon form: each pivot lies to the right of the pivot above it, with zeros below each pivot.

The corresponding triangular system is

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x-y+z&=4 \\ y&=-1 \\ z&=3\end{aligned}\right..
$$

Back substitution gives

$$
\begin{aligned}z&=3 \\ y&=-1-(0)(3)=-1 \\ x&=4-(-1)(-1)-(1)(3)=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $\langle 0,-1,3\rangle$.
